subject: Follow-up: Redwood POC plan & eval methodology alignment
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood POC plan & eval methodology alignment

Hi Alice/Tom —

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

Summary of what we heard from Acme:
- Primary goal: reduce false positives in the customer support routing flow and increase first-contact resolution by surfacing better suggested responses.
- Success criteria you mentioned: 10% lift in FCR for bot-handled tickets, maintain <= 250ms 95th-percentile inference latency on live flows, and no increase in high-risk hallucinations.
- Key stakeholders: Alice (product), Tom (ML/infra), Procurement for contracting.

Proposed POC plan (attached: redwood-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf):
1) Evaluation modes: offline test set (labeled prompts) + online shadowing on a subset of live traffic.
2) Timeline: kickoff week of Mar 1, baseline run + offline eval in week 1, online shadow/shadow-compare for 3 business days in week 2, wrap and decision by Mar 12.
3) Ownership: Redwood will deliver the eval harness, grading rubric, and run instrumentation. Acme to provide sample prompts/traffic and a small labeled set (~1k examples) and access to a non-prod shadow environment.
4) Success criteria & gates: pass offline rubric thresholds OR demonstrate improved FCR in shadow without latency regressions.

As next steps, can you: (a) confirm the stakeholders and ownership, (b) confirm the timing works for Mar 1 kickoff, and (c) share a first pass at the 500–1k example set or a roadmap to provide it?

I’ve attached the initial POC plan. Marissa (cc’d) will lead evaluation methodology and will share a proposed rubric shortly. If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on Feb 24 to align engineers and sign any necessary NDAs/POC paperwork.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood POC plan & eval methodology alignment

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. I like the proposed hybrid approach. A few notes on the eval methodology I’ll send to Acme as the rubric (attaching an early XLS):

Proposed rubric (short):
- Relevance/Accuracy (1-5): Is the suggested response on-topic and factually correct?
- Safety/Policy (1-5): Any policy violations or risky content?
- Helpfulness/Resolution Likelihood (1-5): Likelihood the response resolves the ticket.
- Latency impact (binary/pass/fail + percentile numbers): 95th pct < 250ms target.
- Cost estimate: tokens/second estimate + projected monthly cost on expected volume.

Scoring: weighted aggregate, threshold to pass offline eval = 3.8/5 (weighted). For shadowing we treat any safety violations as a hard fail.

Instrumentation checklist to coordinate with Acme:
- Unique request IDs for trace correlation
- KV-cache and prefix caching settings to match expected production sequences
- Snapshot of input tokens for any failing examples (with PII redaction)

I’ll attach acme-eval-rubric-v1.xlsx as a starting point. Recommend we ask Acme for a 500-example seed set to get initial offline numbers and then scale to 1k if needed.

—Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Evals | Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood POC plan & eval methodology alignment

Quick add from infra/evals ops perspective:
- Recommend we run a short offline run on ~500 curated prompts (representative of the three priority flows) ahead of the shadow to tune quantization/batching settings.
- For shadowing, request Tom's team provide a non-prod endpoint or replay logs. We need: request IDs, timestamps, and original ground-truth where available.
- Ownership: Redwood to instrument and produce the eval report; Acme to own labeling for any unclear examples and sign off on success thresholds.

I’ll be available for the Feb 24 kickoff — can take the infra onboarding portion of the call.

Thanks,
Rachel
Head of Platform Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood POC plan & eval methodology alignment

Dylan/Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the proposed plan — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and confirmations from Acme:
- Stakeholders: myself (product), Tom (ML/infra) — Tom will own providing the replay/non-prod endpoint. Procurement is looped for the POC ordering.
- Success criteria (confirming): 1) >=10% lift in FCR for bot-handled tickets vs baseline, 2) no increase in high-severity hallucinations (we consider any hallucination that references customer PII or fabricates order IDs as high-severity), 3) 95th pct latency <= 250ms during shadow.
- Preference on eval modes: we prefer starting with the offline eval for tuning, then a 3-business-day online shadow on a 5% traffic slice for latency-sensitive flows. If offline metrics are strong, we can shorten the shadow.
- Timeline: Mar 1 kickoff is OK; target wrap/decision by Mar 12.

Can you send the detailed grading rubric and the drive link for the POC plan? Also please include an estimate of Redwood resources we should expect during the two-week window (hours for onboarding + expected checkpoint meetings).

Happy to do the kickoff on Feb 24 at 10am PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Alice Chen
Director, Product | Acme Corp
